data.narrative:
Deep Atomic, a pre-seed nuclear energy company founded by William G.J. Theron, is evaluated against a sector universe of ten nuclear energy companies—three public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and seven private peers including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. The nuclear energy sector contains only six same-sector comparables, but filtering for pre-seed stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier yields fewer than three datapoints in any single category. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of nuclear technology approaches, capital intensity profiles, and deployment timelines across the peer set. No triangulation method produced sufficient data density to support a quantified range.

The inability to anchor to peer multiples or transaction comps reflects the nascent stage of Deep Atomic's development and the limited historical M&A activity in frontier nuclear technologies. Valuation of this company at this stage would require reliance on first-principles methods—pathway to clinical/commercial validation, cash runway, and founder track record—none of which are provided in the available data. A credible range cannot be established without either (1) narrower stage-specific peer data, or (2) detailed financial projections and milestones specific to Deep Atomic.
